where: Section 1, sentence after the ΣνᵢAᵢ = 0 formula
problem: The sentence 'If species i is consumed, νᵢ  0, so its moles rise' has lost its inequality signs and its logic is broken: a consumed species has negative νᵢ and its moles must fall, not rise. As printed, a student reads a contradiction of the sign convention just defined.
fix: If species i is consumed, νᵢ < 0, so its moles fall as ξ grows; if it is formed, νᵢ > 0, so its moles rise.

problem: The formula Xᵢ = −νᵢξ/nᵢ₀ is written in the section on several independent reactions, but it holds only for a single reaction. With r reactions the change in moles of i is Σⱼνᵢⱼξⱼ, so a student applying this formula to the two-reaction case will get the wrong conversion.
fix: State it as the one-reaction result, and add: with several reactions, Xᵢ = (nᵢ₀ − nᵢ)/nᵢ₀ = −(Σⱼ νᵢⱼ ξⱼ)/nᵢ₀.

where: Section 2, paragraph on the range of ξ
problem: Only forward reaction is described (ξ starts at 0 and grows). A reaction written in one direction can run backwards, in which case ξ is negative and products are consumed; the stated bounds do not say this.
fix: Add that ξ is positive when the reaction proceeds as written and negative when it runs in reverse; the only firm limits are that no nᵢ may become negative.
